To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide an information theoretic objective for learning fair representations and demonstrate that a range existing approaches optimize approximated Lagrangian duals of this objective.

we proposed a new information theoretically motivated objective function to learn maximally expressive representations that are subject to fairness constraints, and we demonstrated that a range of state-of-the-art approaches optimize approximations of our objective function.

(1) we propose an information theoretically inspired objective for learning maximized expressive representations that are fair with respect, to a user defined level, to protected attributes; (2) we prove that a range of recent approaches are approximations to the dual of this objective; (3) we propose an algorithm for directly optimizing the objective and demonstrate empirically that our method can learn more expressive representations than existing methods while controlling the level of unfairness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning representations of data that are fair with respect, to some protected attributes.
developing fair and expressive data representations.
the problem of learning fair representations from a data set.
